claims: NASA successfully launched the Artemis II mission on Wednesday, April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II mission lifted off from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B in Florida.
The Artemis II mission marks the first human journey to the moon in over 50 years.
The Artemis II mission has a duration of 10 days.
The crew of the Artemis II mission orbited but did not land on the moon.
The crew of the Artemis II mission consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The goal of the Artemis II mission is a 10-day test flight to certify the Orion capsule for future lunar landings.
